blocks.text: Live streamed firing squad execution ‘absolutely disgusting’, says Watt

Labor cabinet minister, Murray Watt says a planned live streamed execution in the US would be extremely distressing for the public, but won’t commit to legislative change to prevent Australians being able to watch it.
The eSafety commissioner, Julie Inman-Grant has said she does not have powers to “proactively prevent” the stream on 3 December.
Watt tells ABC News Breakfast the government is trying to take “as much action as we can” to deal with rapidly evolving technology.

double quotation markI just find the idea of a public streaming of a firing squad execution absolutely disgusting. When I first heard that was being proposed, I couldn’t believe that it was real. I think all Australians would agree that this is a very distressing thing to have publicised … We’ve seen now that the eSafety Commissioner has said they don’t have those powers. I wouldn’t want to commit to any legislative change at this point in time, but what I do think it shows is this rapidly evolving situation that we’ve got with technology, which is why our government is trying to take as much action as we can, as quickly as we can.”
Ben Doherty
Greens say big tech has been ‘laughing all the way to the bank’ and ‘we need proper regulations’

Sarah Hanson-Young is leading the Greens’ negotiations with the government over legislation designed to hold tech companies responsible for preventing harm to Australians, in particular children. The legislation is expected to be tabled in parliament this week.

Hanson-Young, the Greens’ manager of business in the Senate, said the party would wait to see the details of the legislation before deciding whether to support it. But the senator said the Greens supported the imperative, telling the ABC’s 7:30 program that big tech companies had been “running amok for far too long and we want laws that will actually hold them to account”.
Hanson-Young added:

double quotation markPutting in place a duty of care on these big tech platforms is something that’s well and truly overdue. And these big tech companies, social media platforms have been getting away with profiting off content that has been harmful, of technologies that have been designed to be deliberately addictive, even though they know the harm that that can do. And they’ve just been laughing all the way to the bank. We need proper regulations on these tech companies.

Greens at odds about Ukraine weapons
Australia sending tanks, weapons, infantry and ammunition to Ukraine has put Greens politicians at odds.

Sarah Hanson-Young on Monday said she supported giving Kyiv military aid if that’s what was needed, contradicting her party’s freshly minted leader David Shoebridge during his first sitting week in the top job, who has said Greens policy is not to provide military support – only humanitarian.
“If that’s the support that people need in order to defend themselves from the invasion of Russia, I think Australians need to support that,” Hanson-Young told ABC’s 7.30.

double quotation markWe always come from a position of wanting to de-escalate military violence … we want to see humanitarian support, we want to see diplomatic support, but of course you can’t allow people to be left fending for themselves.

blocks.text: Labor’s $630m funding boost for charities
Sarah Basford Canales

Charities and not-for-profit organisations will receive a $630m funding boost from the federal government after the Fair Work Commission awarded pay rises for health, disability and community services workers.

The government said the funding would go to 128,000 charities and not-for-profit organisations across 92 government programs to cover the wage rises that seek to address historic undervaluing in female-dominated sectors.
The finance minister and minister for women, Katy Gallagher, said:

double quotation markWe cannot close the gender pay gap without ... addressing the historic undervaluation of work performed predominantly by women. Australia’s gender pay gap is at a record low, and this is another significant step towards ensuring women are properly recognised and rewarded for their contribution. This move is also a clear signal to the community that this workforce and the support they provide our community is important and valued.

blocks.caption: Finance minister and minister for women Katy Gallagher. Photograph: Hollie Adams/Reuters
